event: Adobe and Figma sign a definitive merger agreement: about USD 20 billion, roughly half cash and half stock, expected to close in 2023 subject to regulatory approvals
UK CMA launches its Phase 1 merger inquiry
CMA Phase 1 decision: the deal may be expected to result in a substantial lessening of competition unless acceptable undertakings are offered
CMA refers the deal to an in-depth Phase 2 investigation
European Commission opens an in-depth investigation (interactive product design software)
European Commission sends Adobe a Statement of Objections
CMA provisional findings: the deal would eliminate competition in product design, image editing and illustration software; notice of possible remedies, which could include blocking the deal
Adobe and Figma mutually agree to terminate the merger agreement; Adobe to pay Figma the agreed USD 1 billion termination fee within three business days

Termination announced: "no clear path to receive necessary regulatory approvals from the European Commission and the UK Competition and Markets Authority"; the Commission closes its investigation after Adobe withdraws
CMA publishes the cancellation of its merger reference
Figma files its S-1 registration statement for an IPO
Figma lists on the NYSE (FIG) at USD 33 a share and closes its first day at USD 115.50
